summary: Ephemeral healthcheck keys consumed promotional buffer during dedicated->private migration window
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightCourt AI reports that a promotional buffer (USD 2,500 trial credit) was exhausted during a Dedicated->Private migration window. They believe the credits were consumed by automated ephemeral 'healthcheck' invocations from a CI runner that had been re-bound to their org during migration cutover. Impact: Customer now shows a provisional negative balance on their invoice and is blocked from completing the final migration billing reconciliation. Environment: Dedicated cluster (dedicated-gpu-pool-7) transitioning to Private deployment (private-vpc-12) between 2026-03-05 23:45 and 2026-03-06 01:20 UTC. Steps to reproduce / observed sequence: 1) Customer initiated migration; infra automation re-registered some ephemeral CI keys under customer org to validate private endpoint. 2) At cutover a burst of 10k short-lived requests (healthcheck/tool-invoke) hit the hosted fallback and were recorded by the postback-processor. 3) Metering records show these as tool-invoke and warmup tokens attributed to the org's primary cost center. 4) Promotional buffer credits appear to be applied (and then reversed) in short order leaving a net negative provisional balance. Logs / evidence: - Customer provided org-usage-export CSV rows (attached) showing ~10,120 short requests between 2026-03-06T00:00:05Z and 2026-03-06T00:04:20Z. - Postback ID samples: pb_8a3f2c, pb_8a4031, pb_8a40d5 (timestamps included). - Console estimate before finalization: $0 due to buffer. Finalized provisional balance: -$1,374.45. Request: Please audit attribution for the burst, confirm whether ephemeral keys should have consumed the promo buffer, and provide a provisional credit or reversal while we investigate. Customer has asked for a timeline for reversal before final invoice is issued.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Support (Laura Chen): Opened ticket after initial call with BrightCourt. Attached CSV export and partial console snapshots.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Support (Miguel Torres): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to Metering and Billing for urgent audit. Assigned to SRE on-call for the migration window pinning.

2026-03-10 14:45 - SRE (Priya Nair): Initial dig: postback-processor shows 10k short POSTs from edge-proxy-east-1-7 during 00:00-00:05 UTC. Many were classified as tool-invoke due to presence of tool_call header on canary traffic. Suspect CI runner used a service token with org tag.

2026-03-10 16:30 - Billing (Omar Reed): Noted promotional buffer consumption pattern: buffer applied, then proto-reversal due to postback dedupe rule firing. Still leaves net negative because of double-application during two reconciliation passes. Will hold finalization and flag for provisional credit if audit confirms misattribution.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Customer (BrightCourt, T. Malik): Customer confirms CI was re-bound and apologizes — asks for temporary hold on invoice and prefers credit to be applied to migration cost center rather than parent org.
2026-03-11 12:05 - Support (Miguel Torres): Noted customer preference; asked Billing for guidance on cost-center reassignment and provisional waiver timeline.
investigation_notes: SRE trace: edge-proxy logs show CI runner IP 34.215.122.8 using ephemeral key k-ephem-88 which during migration was mistakenly imported into customer master key list.

Postback-processor ran two reconciliation passes: first recorded usage and applied promo buffer; second pass deduped a subset and reversed, but timing led to transient double-application and final negative provisional balance.
Metering team to correlate postback fingerprints with ingestion-time tag (tag namespace: staging-ci) to determine whether these should have been excluded from promo-eligible buckets.
Preliminary conclusion: Not a tokenization bug; attribution and reconciliation ordering bug in postback-processor when handling ephemeral keys during org import.
Related PR for postback fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/postback-service/pull/302 (pending review)
Estimated scope: ~10k requests, ~$1.4k net impact to promotional buffer; potential to affect other customers with similar migration flows — recommend runbook update.
resolution_notes: Billing agreed to place provisional hold on final invoice for BrightCourt while audit completes.
Action item: Billing will issue temporary credit of $1,374.45 to bring provisional balance to $0 pending final reconciliation (actioned 2026-03-12 by Omar Reed).
SRE will backfill a postback patch to exclude staging-ci tagged keys from promo-eligible aggregation and deploy canary 2026-03-13 (PR referenced).
Follow-up: Runbook updated to include org-import checklist to avoid ephemeral key import; outreach to customers with migration activity last 30 days scheduled.
Ticket to be closed after validated ledger adjustment and customer confirmation of receipt of provisional credit.
resolution: Provisional credit issued; engineering fix in review and runbook updated. Pending customer confirmation and final ledger reconciliation.
